/Server/Security/Signing.title: Signing certificates and trust
/Server/Security/Signing.description: Server-side signing settings - shared signature images, the server and organisation certificate, signature validation trust, revocation and timestamp servers.
/Server/Security/Signing.article:
Self-hosted server

Signing certificates and trust

How people use the tools is in the user guide: Sign and Certificate signing.

Signature images#

Signed-in users can keep signatures from the Sign tool on the server. They are stored under customFiles/signatures/:

Folder Filled by Visible to
ALL_USERS/ Admins with Save Shared, or files you copy in Everyone, including when login is off
<username>/ That user with Save Personal, or files you copy in That user only
  • Files you copy in must be PNG or JPEG (.png, .jpg, .jpeg).
  • Each signature can be up to 2 MB. Each user can save up to 20 personal signatures, 20 MB in total. Shared signatures have no count or total limit.
  • In Docker, mount the folder so the files survive updates:
yaml
volumes:
  - ./customFiles:/customFiles

Server certificate Login required#

The server certificate lets users choose Server as the certificate source in Sign with Certificate, so they can sign without a certificate of their own. It is on by default. To turn it off, set system.serverCertificate.enabled: false.

On first start the server creates a self-signed certificate and keeps it in configs/server-certificate.p12. Change it in Settings → Server → System → Certificate Signing, or in settings.yml. Changes apply after a restart.

Setting In the app Default
system.serverCertificate.enabled Enable Certificate Signing true
system.serverCertificate.organizationName Organization Name Stirling PDF Inc
system.serverCertificate.validity Certificate Validity (days) 365
system.serverCertificate.regenerateOnStartup Regenerate on Startup false
Warning

With regenerateOnStartup: true, the server replaces its certificate on every start, including one you uploaded.

Use your organisation's certificate#

To sign with a certificate from your own certificate authority, replace the generated one with a PKCS#12 keystore (.p12 or .pfx). There is no screen for this, so use the admin API with an admin's API key:

bash
curl -X POST https://pdf.example.com/api/v1/admin/server-certificate/upload \
  -H "X-API-KEY: <admin-api-key>" \
  -F "file=@org-signing.p12" \
  -F "password=<keystore-password>"
Request What it does
GET /api/v1/admin/server-certificate/info Subject, issuer and validity of the current certificate
POST /api/v1/admin/server-certificate/generate Replace the current certificate with a new self-signed one
GET /api/v1/admin/server-certificate/certificate Download the public certificate as server-cert.cer

Restart after changing the certificate. Give server-cert.cer to anyone who needs to trust your signatures in other software.

Signature validation trust#

Validate PDF Signature checks each signer's certificate against these trust sources:

yaml
security:
  validation:
    trust:
      serverAsAnchor: true    # certificates from this server
      useSystemTrust: true    # the Java runtime's trust store
      useMozillaBundle: true  # the bundled Mozilla CA list
      useAATL: false          # Adobe Approved Trust List, downloaded at startup
      useEUTL: false          # EU Trusted List (eIDAS), downloaded at startup
    aatl:
      url: https://trustlist.adobe.com/tl.pdf
    eutl:
      lotlUrl: https://ec.europa.eu/tools/lotl/eu-lotl.xml
      acceptTransitional: false  # also trust certificates in the 'supervisionincessation' state
bash
SECURITY_VALIDATION_TRUST_SERVERASANCHOR=true
SECURITY_VALIDATION_TRUST_USESYSTEMTRUST=true
SECURITY_VALIDATION_TRUST_USEMOZILLABUNDLE=true
SECURITY_VALIDATION_TRUST_USEAATL=false
SECURITY_VALIDATION_TRUST_USEEUTL=false
SECURITY_VALIDATION_AATL_URL=https://trustlist.adobe.com/tl.pdf
SECURITY_VALIDATION_EUTL_LOTLURL=https://ec.europa.eu/tools/lotl/eu-lotl.xml
SECURITY_VALIDATION_EUTL_ACCEPTTRANSITIONAL=false
  • Trust sources load at startup, so restart after changing them.
  • To trust your own certificate authority, add it to the Java runtime's trust store.
  • A certificate a user uploads in the tool replaces all of these for that one check.

Revocation checking#

Revocation checks are off by default.

yaml
security:
  validation:
    revocation:
      mode: none      # none, ocsp, crl or ocsp+crl
      hardFail: false
    allowAIA: false   # let the server fetch issuer certificates and revocation data from the network
bash
SECURITY_VALIDATION_REVOCATION_MODE=none
SECURITY_VALIDATION_REVOCATION_HARDFAIL=false
SECURITY_VALIDATION_ALLOWAIA=false
mode What it does
none No revocation check
ocsp Ask the certificate authority's OCSP responder, with no CRL fallback
crl Use certificate revocation lists, with no OCSP fallback
ocsp+crl Try OCSP first, then a CRL

If the revocation status can't be found, hardFail: false lets validation continue and hardFail: true fails it. Checks need outbound access to the OCSP and CRL servers. Only turn on allowAIA where outbound requests from the server are acceptable.

Timestamp servers#

Timestamp PDF only sends a SHA-256 hash of the document to a time stamp authority (TSA). Users can pick DigiCert, Sectigo, SSL.com, FreeTSA, MeSign, or a server you allow:

yaml
security:
  timestamp:
    defaultTsaUrl: http://timestamp.digicert.com   # used when the user doesn't pick one
    customTsaUrls:
      - https://tsa.example.com/timestamp
bash
SECURITY_TIMESTAMP_DEFAULTTSAURL=http://timestamp.digicert.com
SECURITY_TIMESTAMP_CUSTOMTSAURLS=https://tsa.example.com/timestamp   # comma-separated

Any other URL is rejected with "TSA URL is not in the allowed list".

/Server/Security/SSRF-Protection.title: SSRF protection
/Server/Security/SSRF-Protection.description: Stop the server fetching internal addresses or cloud metadata when it loads URLs during conversions, and choose which domains are allowed.
/Server/Security/SSRF-Protection.article:
Self-hosted server

SSRF protection

SSRF protection stops users from making your server fetch addresses they shouldn't reach, such as http://192.168.1.1/admin or the cloud metadata service at http://169.254.169.254/. It applies when the server loads remote content referenced in files it converts, such as HTML, SVG and office documents. Setting system.disableSanitize: true turns these checks off. URL to PDF ignores these settings.

Configure SSRF protection in Settings → Server → Sign-in & security → HTML URL Security, or under system.html.urlSecurity.

Warning

URL to PDF is off by default because of these risks (Enable URL to PDF in Settings → Server → Advanced → Feature Flags, or system.enableUrlToPDF). Only turn it on for internal use.

Settings#

Setting Default What it does
enabled true Turn SSRF protection on or off.
level MEDIUM OFF, MEDIUM or MAX (see below).
allowedDomains [] Domains to allow (see below).
blockedDomains [] Extra domains to block in MEDIUM (see below).
internalTlds .local, .internal, .corp, .home Domain endings treated as internal.
blockPrivateNetworks true Block private ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x).
blockLocalhost true Block 127.x and ::1.
blockLinkLocal true Block 169.254.x and fe80::.
blockCloudMetadata true Block cloud provider metadata addresses.
yaml
system:
  html:
    urlSecurity:
      enabled: true
      level: MEDIUM
      allowedDomains: []
      blockedDomains: []
bash
SYSTEM_HTML_URLSECURITY_ENABLED=true
SYSTEM_HTML_URLSECURITY_LEVEL=MEDIUM
SYSTEM_HTML_URLSECURITY_ALLOWEDDOMAINS=     # comma-separated
SYSTEM_HTML_URLSECURITY_BLOCKEDDOMAINS=     # comma-separated

Protection levels#

  • MEDIUM (default) blocks private IPs, localhost, cloud metadata and internal domain endings, and allows the public internet.
  • MAX only allows domains listed in allowedDomains.
  • OFF does no checks. Use it only if your network blocks these requests elsewhere.

Allow and block lists#

  • allowedDomains: in MEDIUM, a non-empty list restricts access to those domains and their subdomains, and the other MEDIUM checks still apply. It doesn't keep the rest of the internet open. In MAX, a host must match an entry exactly, so list each subdomain.
  • blockedDomains: only used in MEDIUM, with exact matching. Blocking example.com doesn't block sub.example.com.

/Server/Storage/Database.title: Database
/Server/Storage/Database.description: Back up and restore the built-in H2 database, or connect Stirling PDF to your own PostgreSQL database.
/Server/Storage/Database.article:
Self-hosted server

Database

Stirling PDF keeps users, teams and activity records in a database: a built-in H2 database by default, or your own PostgreSQL server. Both are managed in Settings → Server → Database.

Built-in database#

The database file is configs/stirling-pdf-DB-2.3.232.mv.db (the number is the H2 version). In Docker, mount /configs as a volume or it is lost when the container is replaced.

Backups#

The server exports the built-in database as a SQL file every day at midnight, and again after changes to user accounts. Backups are saved as backup_*.sql in configs/backup/db/. Older ones are deleted automatically, leaving the six most recent.

To change the schedule, set system.databaseBackup.cron (SYSTEM_DATABASEBACKUP_CRON) to a six-field cron expression that starts with seconds. The default is 0 0 0 * * ?.

In Settings → Server → Database → Backups & Restore you can create, download, delete and restore backups. Import next to a listed backup restores it straight away. Upload & import restores a .sql file you choose and asks for a confirmation code first.

Warning

Importing a backup replaces all current data. Keep copies of the backup folder off the server.

Backups and restores are only available for the built-in database. With an external database, use your database's own backup tools.

With an Enterprise licence and email set up, the server can email admins about backups and imports:

yaml
premium:
  enterpriseFeatures:
    databaseNotifications:
      backups:
        successful: false
        failed: false
      imports:
        successful: false
        failed: false
bash
PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_DATABASENOTIFICATIONS_BACKUPS_SUCCESSFUL=false
PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_DATABASENOTIFICATIONS_BACKUPS_FAILED=false
PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_DATABASENOTIFICATIONS_IMPORTS_SUCCESSFUL=false
PREMIUM_ENTERPRISEFEATURES_DATABASENOTIFICATIONS_IMPORTS_FAILED=false

External database#

Use PostgreSQL instead of the built-in database, for example to share one database across clustered servers or to use your existing backup tooling. It needs a build with login and a Team or Enterprise licence. Without one, a server using an external database refuses to process files; sign-in, settings and licence activation still work (Plans and licences).

The new database starts empty. If the server already has users, read Switch an existing server first.

Set it in Settings → Server → Database → Connection, or in settings.yml, then restart:

yaml
system:
  datasource:
    enableCustomDatabase: true
    customDatabaseUrl: jdbc:postgresql://db.example.com:5432/stirling_pdf
    username: stirling
    password: your-database-password
bash
SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_ENABLECUSTOMDATABASE=true
SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_CUSTOMDATABASEURL=jdbc:postgresql://db.example.com:5432/stirling_pdf
SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=stirling
SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=your-database-password

When customDatabaseUrl is set, the server ignores the separate connection fields. To build the URL from parts instead, leave it empty and set:

Setting Default What it is
type postgresql postgresql or h2
hostName localhost Database host, or the database container's service name in Docker
port 5432 Database port
name postgres Database name

Docker Compose example#

yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    image: docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
    depends_on:
      - db
    environment:
      SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_ENABLECUSTOMDATABASE: "true"
      SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_CUSTOMDATABASEURL: "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/stirling_pdf"
      SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_USERNAME: "stirling"
      SYSTEM_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD: "change-me"
    # ports, volumes and other settings as usual

  db:
    image: postgres:17.2-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: "stirling_pdf"
      POSTGRES_USER: "stirling"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "change-me"
    volumes:
      - ./postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

Switch an existing server#

Nothing is copied to the new database. Users, teams, API keys and activity records stay in the H2 file, and there is no built-in way to move them to PostgreSQL. Switch before you add users, or plan to recreate them.

  1. Back up the configs/ folder.
  2. Activate your Team or Enterprise licence first. The licence is kept in configs/, not in the database, so it survives the switch. A link to Stirling Cloud is stored in the database, so link the server again afterwards.
  3. Set the connection details as above and restart.
  4. Sign in as admin / stirling, or with the SECURITY_INITIALLOGIN_USERNAME account if you set one (First admin account), then recreate your users and API keys.

To go back, set enableCustomDatabase: false and restart. The server opens the old H2 file in configs/ again, with the data it had before the switch.

/Server/Storage/File-Storage.title: File storage and sharing
/Server/Storage/File-Storage.description: Let users keep files on your server and share them, choose local, database or S3 storage and set quotas.
/Server/Storage/File-Storage.article:
Self-hosted server

File storage and sharing

Login required

Let signed-in users keep files on the server in My Files and share them with each other. How users work with their files is in My files and sharing.

File storage settings#

File storage is on by default. To turn it off, clear Enable Server File Storage in Settings → Server → System → File Storage & Sharing, or set storage.enabled: false:

yaml
storage:
  enabled: true
  provider: local        # local, database or s3
  local:
    basePath: ./storage  # folder for stored files (local provider)
bash
STORAGE_ENABLED=true
STORAGE_PROVIDER=local
STORAGE_LOCAL_BASEPATH=./storage

In Docker, mount the storage folder so files survive container updates:

yaml
volumes:
  - ./stirling-data/storage:/storage

Storage providers#

Provider Plan Where files go
local Any A folder on disk (basePath). Best for most servers and for large files.
database Team or Enterprise The server's database. Keeps everything in one place, but uses more memory with large files.
s3 Team or Enterprise Any S3-compatible object store. Use this for clustered servers.

S3-compatible storage#

yaml
storage:
  enabled: true
  provider: s3
  s3:
    endpoint: ""                  # blank = AWS regional default; otherwise the full URL incl. https://
    bucket: my-bucket             # required
    region: us-east-1
    accessKey: ""                 # blank = AWS default credentials (env vars, profile or instance role)
    secretKey: ""
    pathStyleAccess: false        # true for MinIO and Supabase
    allowPrivateEndpoints: false  # true only for a trusted in-cluster store such as MinIO
    requestChecksumCalculation: WHEN_SUPPORTED   # WHEN_SUPPORTED, WHEN_REQUIRED or DISABLED
    responseChecksumValidation: WHEN_SUPPORTED   # WHEN_SUPPORTED, WHEN_REQUIRED or DISABLED
bash
STORAGE_ENABLED=true
STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3
STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT=""
STORAGE_S3_BUCKET=my-bucket
STORAGE_S3_REGION=us-east-1
STORAGE_S3_ACCESSKEY=""
STORAGE_S3_SECRETKEY=""
STORAGE_S3_PATHSTYLEACCESS=false
STORAGE_S3_ALLOWPRIVATEENDPOINTS=false
STORAGE_S3_REQUESTCHECKSUMCALCULATION=WHEN_SUPPORTED
STORAGE_S3_RESPONSECHECKSUMVALIDATION=WHEN_SUPPORTED
  • allowPrivateEndpoints: false makes the server refuse to start if endpoint resolves to a private, loopback or link-local address.
  • Set requestChecksumCalculation: WHEN_REQUIRED if uploads fail with an unsupported x-amz-checksum-* header. Set responseChecksumValidation: WHEN_REQUIRED if downloads report false checksum mismatches.
Provider endpoint region pathStyleAccess Notes
AWS S3 blank your region false
MinIO (in-cluster) http://minio:9000 us-east-1 true Also set allowPrivateEndpoints: true.
Cloudflare R2 https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com auto false If uploads fail with a checksum header error, set requestChecksumCalculation: WHEN_REQUIRED.
Supabase Storage https://<project>.supabase.co/storage/v1/s3 your project region true
Backblaze B2 https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com your region false On B2 accounts older than July 2025, set requestChecksumCalculation: WHEN_REQUIRED if uploads fail.
DigitalOcean Spaces https://<region>.digitaloceanspaces.com your region false 5 GB limit per object.

Turn on sharing#

Sharing needs storage. Use the toggles in File Storage & Sharing, or:

yaml
storage:
  sharing:
    enabled: true            # Enable Sharing
    linkEnabled: true        # Enable Share Links, needs system.frontendUrl
    emailEnabled: false      # Enable Email Sharing, needs mail and share links
    linkExpirationDays: 3    # days before a share link expires

system:
  frontendUrl: https://pdf.example.com   # used to build share links
bash
STORAGE_SHARING_ENABLED=true
STORAGE_SHARING_LINKENABLED=true
STORAGE_SHARING_EMAILENABLED=false
STORAGE_SHARING_LINKEXPIRATIONDAYS=3
SYSTEM_FRONTENDURL=https://pdf.example.com
  • Share links still require the recipient to sign in. There is no anonymous access.
  • Email sharing needs email set up and share links turned on. Sharing with an email address that has no account sends that person a share link.
  • Expired links and orphaned files are cleaned up once a day.

Quotas#

yaml
storage:
  quotas:
    maxStorageMbPerUser: -1   # per-user limit in MB
    maxStorageMbTotal: -1     # limit for the whole server in MB
    maxFileMb: -1             # largest single stored file in MB
bash
STORAGE_QUOTAS_MAXSTORAGEMBPERUSER=-1
STORAGE_QUOTAS_MAXSTORAGEMBTOTAL=-1
STORAGE_QUOTAS_MAXFILEMB=-1

-1 means no limit. When a file is replaced, only the change in size counts.

Troubleshooting#

Message Fix
"Storage is disabled" Set storage.enabled: true and check login is on.
"Share links are disabled" Set storage.sharing.linkEnabled: true and system.frontendUrl.
"Email sharing is disabled" Set storage.sharing.emailEnabled: true and set up email.
"Share links must be enabled for email sharing" Turn on share links as well.
Share link returns 404 The link has expired or was revoked. The owner needs to create a new one.
Upload rejected with 413 A quota was reached. Raise the limit or delete files.

To manage stored files with scripts, use the /api/v1/storage endpoints listed in your server's API reference (REST API).

/Server/Storage/Folder-Scanning.title: Folder scanning
/Server/Storage/Folder-Scanning.description: Process files automatically by dropping them into a watched folder on the server alongside a pipeline JSON file exported from Automate.
/Server/Storage/Folder-Scanning.article:
Self-hosted server

Folder scanning

Folder scanning runs a saved workflow on every file dropped into a watched folder on the server. Each job folder holds one pipeline JSON file, and the server processes new files in it once a minute. No one needs to be signed in.

Folder scanning runs on self-hosted servers only. It isn't part of the desktop app. For a saved, monitored workflow with a folder trigger, see the Processor's Sources and Pipelines.

Input files are deleted

After a successful run, the input files are deleted from the job folder. Keep a copy of any originals you need.

1. Export the pipeline#

Build the workflow with the Automate tool (Automate) and select Export for Folder Scanning. This downloads <name>.folder-scan.json. The plain Export button produces a different format that only works for importing back into Automate.

You can also write the file by hand. Each step names an API operation and its parameters. outputDir and outputFileName control where results go, and folder scanning needs both. A minimal file:

json
{
  "name": "Compress invoices",
  "pipeline": [
    { "operation": "/api/v1/misc/compress-pdf", "parameters": { "optimizeLevel": 5 } }
  ],
  "outputDir": "{outputFolder}",
  "outputFileName": "{filename}-{date}"
}

The format and operations are described in Pipeline API, including filters that skip files which don't match.

2. Create a job folder#

Make a subfolder in the watched folder for each workflow, put its JSON file in it, then drop files next to the JSON:

pipeline/
├── watchedFolders/
│   └── invoices/
│       ├── compress-invoices.folder-scan.json
│       ├── invoice-001.pdf
│       └── invoice-002.pdf
└── finishedFolders/
  • The watched folder is /pipeline/watchedFolders in Docker, or pipeline/watchedFolders next to a JAR. Mount /pipeline as a volume to reach it from the host.
  • Only subfolders are job folders. Files dropped straight into watchedFolders are never processed.
  • The server uses the first .json file it finds in a job folder, so keep one per folder. A folder with no .json file is skipped.

How files are processed#

  • Files still being copied in are skipped and picked up on a later check.
  • Files whose type the workflow can't accept are skipped and left in place.
  • While a file is being processed it sits in a processing subfolder of the job folder.

Results and file names#

Results go to outputDir. Exported files set it to {outputFolder}, the finished folder (/pipeline/finishedFolders in Docker), and outputFileName to {filename}.

  • outputDir accepts {outputFolder} (the finished folder) and {folderName} (the job folder).
  • outputFileName accepts {filename}, {pipelineName}, {date} (yyyyMMdd) and {time} (HHmmss).

With the exported defaults, every result lands in the same folder and a later file with the same name overwrites an earlier one. Add {date} and {time} to outputFileName, or {folderName} to outputDir, to keep them apart.

Errors#

  • If the workflow reports an error, the files move to an error subfolder of the job folder. Fix the cause, then move them back to retry.
  • If processing stops unexpectedly, the files stay in the processing subfolder. Move them back to the job folder to retry.
  • If nothing happens, wait at least a minute, check the server can read and write the folders, and look for errors in the server log (for example docker logs stirling-pdf).

Folder settings#

Change the folders in Settings → Server → System → Custom Paths, under Pipeline Directories. Enter one path per line, or separate them with commas, in Watched Folders Directories. Changes apply after a restart.

Setting Default What it does
system.customPaths.pipeline.pipelineDir pipeline Base folder for the watched and finished folders.
system.customPaths.pipeline.watchedFoldersDirs [] List of watched folders. Every entry is scanned.
system.customPaths.pipeline.watchedFoldersDir <pipelineDir>/watchedFolders A single watched folder.
system.customPaths.pipeline.finishedFoldersDir <pipelineDir>/finishedFolders Where results go.
autoPipeline.fileReadiness.enabled true Wait until a file has finished being written before processing it.
autoPipeline.fileReadiness.settleTimeMillis 5000 How long a file must be unchanged before it counts as complete.
autoPipeline.fileReadiness.sizeCheckDelayMillis 500 Pause between two size checks when detecting a file still being written.
autoPipeline.fileReadiness.allowedExtensions [] Only process these extensions, without the dot, such as ["pdf", "tiff"]. Empty accepts all.
Check the startup log

A watched folder that is the same as the finished folder, or inside it, logs a CRITICAL processing-loop error. Nested watched folders, or a finished folder inside a watched folder, log warnings.

/Server/Storage/Google-Drive.description: Let users open files from Google Drive in Stirling PDF by connecting a Google Cloud project to your server.
/Server/Storage/Google-Drive.article:
Self-hosted server

Google Drive file picker

Let users pick files from their Google Drive when opening files in Stirling PDF. It works on every plan.

1. Set up Google Cloud#

  1. Create or choose a Google Cloud project, following Setting up your environment in Google's Picker API guide.
  2. In Credentials, select Create credentials → OAuth client ID. Add your Stirling PDF address (for example https://pdf.example.com) to the client's Authorized JavaScript origins.
  3. In the same place, select Create credentials → API key.
  4. Note your project number from IAM & Admin settings. This is the app ID.

2. Configure Stirling PDF#

Enter the values in Settings → Server → Integrations → Google Drive, or in settings.yml:

yaml
premium:
  proFeatures:
    googleDrive:
      enabled: true
      clientId: <client-id>   # the OAuth client ID
      apiKey: <api-key>       # the API key
      appId: <app-id>         # the project number
bash
PREMIUM_PROFEATURES_GOOGLEDRIVE_ENABLED=true
PREMIUM_PROFEATURES_GOOGLEDRIVE_CLIENTID=<client-id>
PREMIUM_PROFEATURES_GOOGLEDRIVE_APIKEY=<api-key>
PREMIUM_PROFEATURES_GOOGLEDRIVE_APPID=<app-id>

/Server/Upgrading.title: Upgrading from V1
/Server/Upgrading.description: Back up, upgrade and check a self-hosted server moving from Stirling PDF V1 to V2 or later, and roll back if you need to.
/Server/Upgrading.article:
Self-hosted server

Upgrading from V1

Settings, users, API keys and the database carry over, but the database is upgraded in place, so back up first. These steps take a V1 server straight to the current release.

Before you upgrade#

  1. Read Breaking changes, especially if you customised the UI, disabled tools by ID, use SAML or run the JAR.

  2. Write down the exact V1 image tag or JAR version you run now, in case you need to roll back.

  3. Stop the server and back up:

    • the configs folder, which holds settings.yml, custom_settings.yml, the built-in database and any licence file
    • customFiles, pipeline and any extra OCR language files
    • your external database, with its own backup tool
    bash
    # Bind mount
cp -a ./configs ./configs-v1-backup
# Named volume or no mount
docker cp stirling-pdf:/configs ./configs-v1-backup

  4. If you can, try the upgrade on a copy of this data first.

Upgrade#

Docker#

Point your compose file at the current image, keeping your volumes and environment variables:

yaml
services:
  stirling-pdf:
    image: docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:latest
bash
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Use latest-fat or latest-ultra-lite if that's the variant you ran, or pin a version tag. See Install with Docker.

JAR#

  1. Install Java 25. V1 ran on Java 17.
  2. Stop the V1 server.
  3. Download the new JAR from GitHub Releases: Stirling-PDF-with-login.jar if you use login, otherwise Stirling-PDF.jar.
  4. Replace the old JAR and start it from the same folder, so it finds configs/.

See Install with Java (JAR).

What happens on first start#

  • settings.yml is rewritten in the current format. Your values are kept, new settings get defaults and removed ones are dropped. See Settings changes.
  • The database is upgraded in place.
  • The free user limit becomes 5 or your current number of users, whichever is higher. It can't change after that.
  • Existing single sign-on users can keep using SAML without an Enterprise licence.
  • Everyone has to sign in again once.

After upgrading#

Check that:

  • admins and users can sign in, including through SSO
  • Settings → Workspace → Usage & Billing shows the plan and user limit you expect
  • tools you disabled are still disabled (see Settings changes if one came back)
  • your API integrations and any branding still work

Roll back#

  1. Stop the server.

  2. Move the upgraded config aside and restore your backup:

    bash
    mv ./configs ./configs-after-upgrade
cp -a ./configs-v1-backup ./configs

  3. If you use an external database, restore its pre-upgrade backup.

  4. Start the V1 image tag or JAR you noted before upgrading.

Don't start V1 against a database the new version has already upgraded.

/Server/Upgrading/Breaking-Changes.title: Breaking changes
/Server/Upgrading/Breaking-Changes.description: Changes since V1 that can break a self-hosted setup, and what to do about each one.
/Server/Upgrading/Breaking-Changes.article:
Self-hosted server

Breaking changes

Check this list before you upgrade a V1 server. Most servers only need the backup and upgrade steps in Upgrading from V1.

New web interface#

V1 built its pages on the server from templates in customFiles/templates/. V2 is a separate web app, so those templates are ignored.

  • For the app name and logo, use the branding settings in UI and branding.
  • Files in customFiles/static/ still replace built-in files at the same path, but the paths are those of the new app, for example customFiles/static/index.html.
  • For deeper changes you would need to build your own frontend. See Contributing.

Removed and renamed settings#

Some settings were removed or renamed, including ui.appName and the pdf-organizer tool ID. Check Settings changes, especially if you disabled tools with endpoints.toRemove.

Login and Docker images#

  • The latest and latest-fat images always include login and admin features. DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY and DISABLE_ADDITIONAL_FEATURES no longer change this; use security.enableLogin (SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN) to turn login on or off.
  • latest-ultra-lite has no login, users or admin settings.
  • New settings files have login on by default. An upgraded server keeps the enableLogin value from its existing settings.yml.
  • Images named s-pdf still get the same builds, but stirlingtools/stirling-pdf is the main name.

Plans and user limits#

  • The Free plan allows 5 users. An upgraded server keeps its current number of users as its limit if that is higher, but can't add users beyond it without Team or Enterprise.
  • SAML sign-in needs Enterprise. Existing single sign-on users keep it.
  • Some admin features need Team or Enterprise. See Plans and licences.
  • Old enterpriseEdition settings in settings.yml move to premium automatically.

Java 25 for the JAR#

The JAR now needs Java 25 instead of Java 17. Docker images include the right Java.

Database#

The built-in and external databases are upgraded in place on first start, so rolling back needs your backup. See Roll back.

API#

API paths still start with /api/v1, and users' API keys carry over. If you generate clients from the OpenAPI spec, regenerate them from /v1/api-docs and test your integrations before switching. See REST API.

/Server/Upgrading/Settings-Changes.title: Settings changes
/Server/Upgrading/Settings-Changes.description: How settings.yml is migrated from V1, which settings were removed or renamed, and which new ones to review.
/Server/Upgrading/Settings-Changes.article:
Self-hosted server

Settings changes

You don't need to edit settings.yml by hand to upgrade. The server updates it on every start, keeps your values and adds new settings with their defaults. If the file has fewer than 31 lines, the server saves it as a .bak and starts from the defaults, so put short overrides in custom_settings.yml or environment variables instead. See settings.yml.

Environment variables still override the file. A variable for a removed setting does nothing.

Removed and renamed settings#

V1 setting Now
enterpriseEdition.* premium.*, moved automatically
premium.proFeatures.CustomMetadata.* premium.proFeatures.customMetadata.*, moved automatically
premium.proFeatures.SSOAutoLogin security.ssoAutoLogin, moved automatically
ui.appName, ui.homeDescription Removed. ui.appNameNavbar sets the browser tab title and the issuer name in authenticator apps. The home description has no replacement.
security.jwt.enabled, keyCleanup, keyRetentionDays, secureCookie Removed. Key cleanup is now security.jwt.enableKeyCleanup (default true). Sign-in lifetimes are security.jwt.tokenExpiryMinutes (default 1440) and desktopTokenExpiryMinutes (default 43200, for the desktop app).
security.csrfDisabled Removed
pdf-organizer in endpoints.toRemove rearrange-pages. Change it yourself, or the page reordering tools come back.

Changed defaults#

These only affect a new settings file. An upgraded file keeps your values.

  • security.enableLogin is now true.
  • system.showUpdate and system.showUpdateOnlyAdmin are now true.
  • system.defaultLocale is now empty, which uses the browser language. It was en-US.

New settings to review#

Setting Why it matters
system.backendUrl, system.frontendUrl backendUrl is required for SSO callbacks. frontendUrl is used in invite and share links and when connecting to Stirling Cloud. See OAuth2 / OIDC single sign-on.
system.corsAllowedOrigins Left empty, it allows every origin. List your own origins to restrict it.
security.xFrameOptions With login on, the default DENY stops other sites embedding Stirling PDF.
mail.enableInvites Invite users by email. Needs mail.enabled and login. See Sign-in and security.
security.validation, security.timestamp, system.serverCertificate Signature checking, timestamp servers and the server signing certificate. See Signing certificates and trust.

storage (File storage and sharing) is new and on by default when login is on.

toolRecommendations is new and on by default. With login on, it records which tools each user runs, in your own database. See Analytics and telemetry.

/Tools.title: All tools
/Tools.description: Every tool in the Stirling PDF tool picker, grouped the way the app shows them, with a link to each guide.
/Tools.article:
All tools

Every tool in the app, grouped as the tool picker shows them. To find one fast, type its name in Search tools... at the top of the picker.

Not every tool is available everywhere. In the desktop app, tools with a cloud badge need Stirling Cloud or a server (Where your tools run). On a self-hosted server, an admin can turn tools off (Turn features on or off).

Quick access#

The most-used tools sit at the top of the picker. Each one has a keyboard shortcut (Keyboard shortcuts).

  • PDF Text Editor - edit the existing text and images in a PDF.
  • Page Editor (PDF Multi Tool in the picker) - rotate, reorder, delete, split and insert blank pages.
  • Merge - combine several PDFs into one.
  • Compare - show the text differences between two PDFs.
  • Compress - make a PDF smaller.
  • Convert - convert between PDF and other formats.
  • OCR / Cleanup scans - make scanned PDFs searchable and clean them up.
  • Redact - permanently black out text, areas or whole pages.

Signing#

  • Sign with Certificate - add a digital signature that proves who signed and shows later changes.
  • Timestamp PDF - add an RFC 3161 timestamp that proves when the PDF existed.
  • Sign - add a drawn, typed or image signature.

Document security#

  • Add Password - require a password to open the PDF and restrict what people can do.
  • Add Watermark - put a text or image watermark across the pages.
  • Add Stamp to PDF - add a text or image stamp at a set position.
  • Sanitize - remove JavaScript, embedded files and other risky content.
  • Flatten - turn form fields and other interactive parts into plain page content.
  • Unlock PDF Forms - make read-only form fields editable again.
  • Change Permissions - allow or block printing, copying, editing and other actions.

Verification#

  • Get ALL Info on PDF - show the version, fonts, page sizes, permissions and metadata.
  • Validate PDF Signature - check who signed a PDF and whether it changed afterwards.

Document review#

  • Read - open a PDF in the viewer to read, search, comment and mark it up.
  • Change Metadata - edit the title, author, keywords, dates and other details.
  • Edit Table of Contents - add, nest and reorder bookmarks.

Page formatting#

  • Crop PDF - trim pages to the area you want.
  • Rotate - turn pages.
  • Auto Rotate - detect each page's orientation and turn it upright.
  • Split - split one PDF into several files.
  • Reorganize Pages - rearrange, duplicate or delete pages.
  • Adjust page size/scale - change the page size and how big the content sits on it.
  • Add Page Numbers - number pages in a set position and format.
  • Multi-Page Layout - put several pages on each sheet.
  • Booklet Imposition - order pages for printing and folding into a booklet.
  • PDF to Single Large Page - join all pages into one long page.
  • Manage Attachments - add, extract, rename or delete files embedded in the PDF.
  • Create Portfolio - bundle several files into one PDF portfolio.

Extraction#

  • Extract Pages - save chosen pages as a new PDF.
  • Extract Images - save every image in the PDF to a ZIP file.

Removal#

  • Remove Pages - delete the pages you choose.
  • Remove Blank pages - find and drop pages with little or no content.
  • Remove Annotations - delete all comments, highlights and markup.
  • Remove image - strip every image, for example to shrink the file.
  • Remove Password - unlock a protected PDF when you know its password.
  • Remove Certificate Sign - strip digital signatures so you can edit the file.

Automation#

  • Auto Form Detection - find form fields and make a PDF fillable.
  • Automate - save a chain of tools and run it on any files.
  • Auto Rename PDF File - rename a file from the title found in it.

General#

  • Add Text - type text anywhere on a page.
  • Add image - place an image anywhere on a page.
  • Annotate - highlight, draw, add notes and shapes in the viewer.
  • Form Editor - fill in, add and edit form fields.

Advanced formatting#

  • Adjust Colors/Contrast - change contrast, brightness and saturation.
  • Repair - try to fix a damaged PDF.
  • Detect & Split Scanned Photos - find the photos on a scanned page and save each photo as a separate image.
  • Overlay PDFs - lay one PDF over another.
  • Replace & Invert Color - swap or invert colours, for example for high contrast.

Developer tools#

  • Show Javascript - list any JavaScript inside a PDF.
  • API, Automated Folder Scanning, SSO Guide and Air-gapped Setup link to the matching docs.

AI#

The AI assistant isn't in the tool list. Open it with the Open Stirling AI assistant button in the workspace (AI assistant).

/Tools/FAQ.title: FAQ
/Tools/FAQ.description: Answers for every Stirling PDF product - reporting bugs, getting help, tracking and privacy, where files are processed, and common tool questions.
/Tools/FAQ.article:
User guide

FAQ

For running a server, see the Server FAQ.

Get help#

  • Questions and setup help: the Discord community.
  • Enterprise customers and licensing: support@stirlingpdf.com.
  • Security vulnerabilities: security@stirlingpdf.com, or report a vulnerability on GitHub. Don't post them in a public issue.

How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?#

Open an issue on GitHub and choose Bug Report or Feature Request. For a bug, include the steps, which product and version you use, and:

  • for a self-hosted server, a diagnostics bundle (Diagnostics)
  • for the desktop app, your connection mode and the log files from Data and log locations

Does Stirling PDF track me?#

Usage analytics are opt-in, and Stirling PDF never tracks the content of your documents. When the How we use Cookies banner appears, click No Thanks to allow only essential cookies.

To change your choice later, click Manage next to Cookie Preferences:

  • Stirling Cloud: in Settings → Legal.
  • Desktop app and self-hosted servers: in Settings → About.

On a self-hosted server, your admin decides whether analytics are on at all. If they're off, you won't see the banner (Analytics and telemetry).

Where are my files processed?#

Files in your workspace are kept in your browser, or on your computer in the desktop app. They're only stored on a server if you save them there (My files and sharing).

  • Stirling Cloud: viewing, rearranging pages and managing files happen in your browser. Tools such as compress, OCR and convert send the file to Stirling's servers and return the result. See Files and privacy.
  • Desktop app: in Local Only mode nothing leaves your computer, and a tool that can't run locally is blocked, not uploaded. See Where your tools run.
  • Self-hosted server: tools run on your organisation's server.

Can I remove an existing watermark?#

No. Stirling PDF has no tool to remove a watermark that's already in a PDF.

How do I add a line break in a stamp or watermark?#

Type \n where you want the break in the text of Add Stamp to PDF or Add Watermark.

User guide

Advanced tools

Automation#

Automate#

Chain several tools into a workflow you can save and run again. See Automate.

Auto Rename PDF File#

Renames a PDF from the title found near the start of the document. Run OCR on scans first.

Advanced Formatting#

Adjust Colors/Contrast#

Adjust contrast, brightness and saturation, and the red, green and blue levels, with a live preview.

Replace & Invert Color#

Under Color operation, choose:

  • High contrast - a preset such as white text on black or yellow text on black.
  • Custom - pick your own text and background colours.
  • Invert all colors - a negative of the page, for example for a dark-mode copy.
  • Convert to CMYK - converts colours for professional printing.

Detect & Split Scanned Photos#

Finds each photo on a scanned page and saves it as a separate image. Scan on a plain, light background with a small gap between photos.

Overlay PDFs#

Lays the pages of one or more overlay PDFs over a base PDF.

  1. Under Select Overlay PDF Files, add the overlay PDFs.
  2. Under Select Overlay Mode, choose:
    • Sequential Overlay uses pages from the first overlay until it ends, then the next.
    • Interleaved Overlay takes one page from each overlay in turn.
    • Fixed Repeat Overlay takes a set number of pages from each overlay. Enter the numbers under Overlay Counts (for Fixed Repeat Mode).
  3. Under Select Overlay Position, choose Foreground or Background.

Repair#

Tries to fix a corrupt or damaged PDF, for example one that won't open.

Developer Tools#

Show Javascript - lists any JavaScript embedded in a PDF.

/Tools/Guides/AI-Assistant.title: AI assistant
/Tools/Guides/AI-Assistant.description: Ask the Stirling AI assistant about your PDFs or tell it what to do, and where AI is available in each product.
/Tools/Guides/AI-Assistant.article:
User guide

AI assistant

The AI assistant answers questions about the files in your workspace and runs tools for you when you describe what you want in plain words.

Where it's available#

  • Stirling Cloud: included for signed-in accounts. AI use draws on your team's credits (Plans, credits and billing). Guests are asked to create an account.
  • Desktop app: sign in to Stirling Cloud, or connect to a self-hosted server that has AI turned on (Connection modes). It isn't available in Local Only mode.
  • Self-hosted server: AI is off until an admin sets it up (AI on your server). The admin can also turn off individual capabilities, so you may not see all of them.

Open the assistant#

  1. Add your files to the workspace.
  2. Click Open Stirling AI assistant at the bottom right. The AI Assistant panel opens.
  3. Type in What do you want to do? and click Send message, or pick a suggestion under Get started, such as Compress this document.

The assistant works on the files in your workspace. When it changes a file, the result is saved as a new version of that file. Merged, split or new files are added to the workspace as new files.

What it can do#

Capability What it does
Chat assistant Runs tools when you ask, for example "merge these into one PDF" or "convert this to PDF".
Document questions Answers questions about the content of a PDF, for example "what's the payment deadline?"
Math auditor Checks a document for calculation errors, such as table totals that don't add up.
PDF comment agent Adds review comments to a PDF based on your instructions.
Create PDF from prompt Creates a new PDF from a description.

For what AI sends on Stirling Cloud, see Files and privacy.

/Tools/Guides/Automate.title: Automate
/Tools/Guides/Automate.description: Save a chain of tools as an automation and run it on any files, then export or import it as JSON.
/Tools/Guides/Automate.article:
User guide

Automate

Automate saves a sequence of tools with their settings, so you can run the same steps on any files in one go. Open it from Automate in the left rail, or from the tool picker under Automation.

Create an automation#

  1. Open Automate and click Create New Automation.
  2. Enter an Automation Name. You can also add a description and choose an Icon.
  3. Click Add Tool and choose a tool in Select a tool.... Click its Configure tool button, set the options and click Save Configuration.
  4. Repeat for each step. Tools run in the order you add them, and you can use the same tool more than once. A tool you haven't set up shows ! Not Configured.
  5. Click Save Automation. It stays disabled until the automation has a name and every tool is configured.

Your automation now appears under Saved. Suggested has ready-made automations, such as Email Preparation and Pre-publish Sanitization. Run one as it is, or choose Copy to Saved from its menu to change it.

Interactive tools, such as PDF Text Editor, Sign, Annotate and Compare, can't be added to an automation.

Run an automation#

Before you start: in the desktop app, sign in to Stirling Cloud or a self-hosted server. On Stirling Cloud, each run uses your team's credits (Plans, credits and billing).

  1. Add the files to your workspace.
  2. In Automate, click the automation.
  3. Click Run Automation. Each step shows its progress.
  4. Review the files under Automation Results, then click Finish.

Edit, export or import#

Open the menu on a saved automation to Edit, Delete or export it:

  • Export downloads <name>.automate.json, which you can import into Stirling PDF elsewhere.
  • Export for Folder Scanning downloads <name>.folder-scan.json for folder scanning on a self-hosted server (Folder scanning) and for the Pipeline API.

Saved automations are kept in this browser. Export them to move them to another browser or computer.

To import, open the menu on Create New Automation and choose Import. Drop a JSON file or paste its contents, then click Import. Both export formats work. If an operation in the file can't be matched to a tool, it's listed as Unmapped.

/Tools/Guides/Compare.article:
User guide

Compare

Compare shows the wording changes between two versions of a PDF. Removed words are highlighted in red and added words in green. The comparison runs on your device, so the files are not uploaded.

Compare two PDFs#

  1. In Compare, under Original PDF, pick the older version.
  2. Under Edited PDF, pick the newer version. Use Swap if you picked them the wrong way round.
  3. Click Compare.

Review the result#

The Additions and Deletions dropdowns list every change. Pick one to jump to it, or search the list.

Limitations#

  • Compare checks extracted text only. Layout, formatting and image changes are not detected.
  • A PDF with no text layer can't be compared. For scanned documents, run OCR on both files first.

/Tools/Guides/Compress.article:
User guide

Compress

Compress a PDF#

  1. Select one or more PDFs and open Compress.
  2. Under Compression Method, choose:
    • Quality - drag the Quality Adjustment slider from 1 to 9 (default 5). Higher levels give smaller files but can blur images.
    • File Size - enter a Desired File Size in KB or MB. Stirling PDF gets as close as it can.
  3. Set any options below, then click Compress.

Options#

Option What it does
Apply Grayscale for Compression Converts images to shades of grey.
Linearize PDF for fast web viewing Reorders the file so the first page shows before the whole file has downloaded.
Convert images to line art Reduces pages to high-contrast black and white for the biggest saving. Not for photos.

When line art is on, two more settings appear:

  • Detail level (1-5, default 3) - how much of the page turns black.
  • Edge emphasis - Gentle, Balanced or Strong (default) edge detection.

If Convert images to line art is greyed out, it isn't available where the tool runs.

If a scan needs to be searchable, run OCR before you compress it.

/Tools/Guides/Content-Editing.description: Edit text, add images, text and stamps, pull out or remove content, and change a PDF's metadata and bookmarks.
/Tools/Guides/Content-Editing.article:
User guide

Content and editing

PDF Text Editor#

PDF Text Editor lets you edit the existing text and images of a PDF. Click Save PDF to apply your changes to the file in your workspace, or Download to save a copy.

Warning

Fonts and layout can shift slightly, so check the result and keep your original.

Images#

  • Add image - upload a PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF or SVG file, then click anywhere on the page to place it. Click Apply Images when you're done.
  • Extract Images - saves every image in the PDF to a ZIP file. Choose the image format to convert them to, and tick Save duplicate images to keep repeats.

To split a scan of several photos into separate images, use Detect & Split Scanned Photos.

Stamps & annotations#

  • Add Text - type your text, click on the page to place it, then click Apply Text.
  • Add Stamp to PDF - add a text or image stamp. Set its position (or drag it in the preview), size, rotation, opacity and margin. Stamp text can include dynamic variables such as the current date, the file name or the page number.
  • Annotate - highlight, draw, and add notes and shapes in the viewer. See Read and annotate.

Remove content#

  • Remove image - strips every image from the PDF.
  • Remove Annotations - deletes all comments, highlights and markup.

Document details#

  • Change Metadata - edit the standard fields (author, title, subject, keywords, creator, producer, creation and modification dates), add your own fields under Custom Metadata, or tick Delete all metadata to strip them.
  • Edit Table of Contents - add, nest and reorder bookmarks in the Bookmark editor. Click Load from selected PDF to start from the existing bookmarks, and use Import JSON or Download JSON to reuse an outline. Click Apply table of contents to save.

/Tools/Guides/Convert.title: Convert
/Tools/Guides/Convert.description: Convert Office files, images, web pages, email, eBooks and comics to PDF, and PDFs to other formats.
/Tools/Guides/Convert.article:
User guide

Convert

Convert a file#

  1. Select one or more files and open Convert.
  2. Convert from is filled in from the files you selected. Pick the target format under Convert to.
  3. Set any options for that conversion, then click Convert Files.

If you select files of different types, they are all converted to PDF.

Convert to PDF#

Type Formats
Office DOCX, DOC, ODT, XLSX, XLS, ODS, PPTX, PPT, ODP, TXT, RTF
Images JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WEBP, SVG
Web and text HTML (or a ZIP with the HTML and its CSS and images), Markdown
Email EML, MSG (Outlook)
eBook EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2
Comics CBZ, CBR

Image options: Color Type (Color, Grayscale or Black & White), Fit Option (Maintain Aspect Ratio, Fit Document to Page or Fill Page), Auto Rotate, and Combine Images to put all images in one PDF instead of one PDF each.

Convert from PDF#

Type Formats
Office DOCX, ODT, PPTX, ODP, XLSX, CSV
Text TXT, RTF, Markdown
Images PNG, JPG, GIF, TIFF, BMP, WEBP
Web HTML, XML
Standards PDF/A (archiving), PDF/X (print), PDF/UA (accessible)
eBook and comics EPUB, AZW3, CBZ, CBR

Notes on some targets:

  • Images - set Color Type, DPI (72-600, default 300) and Output: Multiple (default) for one image per page, or Single for one image containing all pages.
  • Word, PowerPoint and Excel - run OCR on scans first.
  • PDF/A - pick the level (default PDF/A-2b). Strict Mode stops with an error if the result does not fully conform. Digital signatures are removed.
  • PDF/UA - tags the PDF for screen readers. Add a description for each image, or the file comes back tagged but not certified.

A few conversions, such as PDF to PostScript, EPS, PCL or XPS, have no option in Convert. They are available through the REST API.

In the desktop app, some conversions need Stirling Cloud or a server (Where your tools run).

/Tools/Guides/Fill-Form.title: Fill forms
/Tools/Guides/Fill-Form.description: Fill in PDF forms, add or edit form fields, export form data, and detect fields automatically.
/Tools/Guides/Fill-Form.article:
User guide

Fill forms

Open a PDF and select Form Editor, then choose a Form editor mode: Fill, Create or Modify. A PDF with no fields opens in Create.

Fill in a form#

  1. In Fill, click each field on the page (or in the field list) and enter a value.
  2. Turn on Flatten after filling to lock the answers into the page.
  3. Click Save or press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac) to write the values into the PDF. Required fields must be filled first.

To export the entered values, click JSON, CSV or XLSX. If fields don't show up correctly, click Re-scan fields.

Add fields#

  1. Switch to Create.
  2. Pick a field type (Text, Checkbox, Dropdown, List box, Radio, Button or Signature), then draw it on the page. Press Esc to stop drawing.
  3. Click Add n field(s) to PDF.

A Signature field is only a placeholder that marks where a signature belongs. To sign, use Sign or Certificate signing.

Edit fields#

In Modify, select a field to change its properties, drag it to a new position, or delete it. Click Save n change(s) when you're done.

Detect fields automatically#

Auto Form Detection finds text fields, checkboxes and signature areas in a flat PDF and makes them fillable.

  1. In Auto Form Detection, choose a Detection sensitivity: Strict, Balanced (recommended) or Thorough.
  2. Click Detect form fields and review the result. If nothing is found, undo, switch to Thorough and run it again.

If Auto Form Detection is greyed out, the server has no detection model or it was turned off. The ultra-lite image and the JAR downloads can't run it at all. See Tools that are off by default for the admin steps.

To lock or unlock form fields, use Flatten or Unlock PDF Forms (Signing and security tools).

/Tools/Guides/Mobile-Scanner.title: Mobile scanner
/Tools/Guides/Mobile-Scanner.description: Scan documents with your phone camera and send them straight into Stirling PDF with a QR code.
/Tools/Guides/Mobile-Scanner.article:
User guide

Mobile scanner

Scan from your phone#

  1. On your computer, click the QR code button (Upload from Mobile) next to Add Files (Open Files in the desktop app), or From your phone in the file picker.
  2. Scan the QR code with your phone's camera and open the link.
  3. Choose an upload method:
    • Camera - photograph each page. Edge detection finds the page and crops it for you. Use Retake or Add More as needed.
    • File Upload - pick existing photos on the phone.
  4. Tap Upload. The files appear on your computer.
  • Camera needs a secure (HTTPS) connection. If the phone says camera access requires HTTPS, use File Upload instead, or ask your admin to serve Stirling PDF over HTTPS.
  • The QR code button is hidden when you open Stirling PDF on a phone. If you don't see it on a computer, the mobile scanner is turned off. On a self-hosted server an admin can turn it on (Mobile scanner settings).

In the desktop app#

  • Your phone and computer must be on the same network (Wi-Fi).
  • The phone page has no edge detection or auto-crop, so crop your photos before uploading.
  • The phone page also accepts PDFs.

/Tools/Guides/OCR.title: OCR
/Tools/Guides/OCR.description: Make scanned PDFs searchable and selectable, and clean up scans, with OCR.
/Tools/Guides/OCR.article:
User guide

OCR

OCR (optical character recognition) finds the text in scanned or photographed pages and adds it to the PDF, so you can search, select and copy it.

Run OCR#

  1. Select one or more PDFs and open OCR / Cleanup scans.
  2. Under Languages, choose every language that appears in the document. At least one is required.
  3. Pick an OCR Mode and any Processing Options (below).
  4. Click Process OCR and Review, check the result, and download it.

Options#

OCR Mode

  • Auto (skip text layers) - the default. Skips pages that already have text.
  • Force (re-OCR all, replace text) - OCRs every page and replaces any existing text.
  • Strict (abort if text found) - stops if any page already has selectable text.

Processing Options

Option What it does
Compatibility Mode Makes larger files that work better with some languages and older PDF software.
Create a text file Also saves the recognised text as a separate .txt file.
Deskew pages Straightens tilted pages before recognition.
Clean input file Removes noise and boosts contrast before recognition.
Clean final output Tidies the text layer in the finished PDF.

In the desktop app, OCR usually needs Stirling Cloud or a server (Where your tools run). On a self-hosted server, if a language is missing, ask your admin (OCR languages).

/Tools/Guides/Page-Operations.title: Page operations
/Tools/Guides/Page-Operations.description: Merge, split, reorder, rotate, remove, resize and lay out the pages of your PDFs.
/Tools/Guides/Page-Operations.article:
User guide

Page operations

To edit pages visually with thumbnails, see Workspace and Page Editor.

Merge#

Merge joins two or more PDFs into one, in the order shown. Drag files to reorder them, or use Sort By (File Name or Date Modified, ascending or descending). Options:

  • Generate table of contents in the merged file? adds clickable bookmarks named after the original files.
  • Remove digital signature in the merged file? strips signatures, which merging breaks anyway.

Create Portfolio is the alternative when the files should stay separate: it bundles them into one PDF portfolio, whatever their type.

Split#

Split breaks one PDF into several files. Choose a method:

Method Splits
Page Numbers After each page you enter. 3,7 gives pages 1-3, 4-7 and 8 to the end. A range splits after every page in it
Chapters At each bookmark, using the document's outline
Sections Each page into a grid of horizontal and vertical pieces, for example halves or quarters
File Size Into parts under a maximum size, for example 10MB
Page Count Into files with a set number of pages each
Document Count Into a set number of files
Page Divider At QR code divider sheets placed between documents when scanning a batch
Printable Chunks Each oversized page into tiles of a standard paper size (A4, Letter and so on) for printing as a poster

Reorder and rotate#

  • Reorganize Pages - rearrange, duplicate or delete pages. Choose an Organization mode, for example Custom Page Order (enter an order such as 1,3,2,4-6), Reverse Order, Duplex Sort (for scans of all fronts then all backs), Odd-Even Split, Odd-Even Merge or Duplicate all pages.
  • Rotate - turns all pages by 90-degree steps with Rotate Counterclockwise and Rotate Clockwise.
  • Auto Rotate - detects each page's orientation and turns it upright, then shows a report of what it changed. Detection method is Auto, Text only or OCR only. Tick Rotate low confidence pages to match to turn blank or nearly blank pages the same way as the rest.

Remove and extract pages#

  • Extract Pages - copies the pages you enter into a new PDF, in order.
  • Remove Pages - deletes the pages you enter.
  • Remove Blank pages - finds and removes pages with little or no content. Tick Include detected blank pages to also get a PDF of the removed pages so you can check them.

In Extract Pages and Remove Pages, enter single pages and ranges such as 1,3,5-8, or expressions such as 2n-1 (odd pages).

Page size and layout#

  • Adjust page size/scale - choose a Target Page Size (A0-A6, Letter, Legal or Keep Original Size) and a Scale Factor for the content. Page orientation (Portrait or Landscape) sets which way round the chosen size is used. It is unavailable with Keep Original Size.
  • Crop PDF - drag the crop area on the preview, or click Auto-crop whitespace, then Apply Crop.
  • Multi-Page Layout - places several pages on each sheet, in a grid of rows and columns, with optional borders.
  • PDF to Single Large Page - stacks every page into one tall page.
  • Booklet Imposition - reorders and lays out pages so that, printed double-sided and folded, they read in order.

Add to pages#

  • Add Page Numbers - choose the position, which pages to number, the starting number and a custom format such as Page {n}. Zero-pad Width (Bates Stamping) pads numbers to a fixed width, for example 001.
  • Manage Attachments - add, extract, rename or delete files embedded in the PDF.

/Tools/Guides/Redact.title: Redact
/Tools/Guides/Redact.description: Permanently remove sensitive text and areas from a PDF, automatically or by hand.
/Tools/Guides/Redact.article:
User guide

Redact

Redact permanently deletes sensitive text and areas from a PDF, not just hides them. Keep a copy of the original.

Automatic redaction#

  1. Under Redaction Method, choose Automatic.
  2. Under Words to Redact, type a word or phrase and click Add. Repeat for each one.
  3. (Optional) Under Advanced, set:
    • Use Regex - treat each entry as a regular expression.
    • Whole Word Search - match whole words only, so "John" doesn't match "Johnson".
    • Box Color and Custom Extra Padding - the look of the redaction boxes.
    • Convert PDF to PDF-Image - turns the redacted pages into images so no text at all remains behind the boxes. The text is then no longer selectable or searchable.
  4. Click Redact.

Automatic mode can redact several files at once: select them in the file manager first.

Patterns for personal data#

With Use Regex on, try these patterns:

Type Example pattern
US Social Security number \d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}
Credit or debit card \d{4}[ -]?\d{4}[ -]?\d{4}[ -]?\d{4}
IBAN [A-Z]{2}\d{2}[A-Z0-9]{1,30}
US routing number (ABA) \b\d{9}\b
Labelled account number [Aa]ccount\s*#?\s*\d{6,}
Email address [\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+
US phone number \(\d{3}\)\s*\d{3}-\d{4}
Date (YYYY-MM-DD) \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}

Manual redaction#

  1. Under Redaction Method, choose Manual. The document opens in the viewer.
  2. Set the Redaction Color.
  3. Select text, or draw an area over images, signatures or anything else, to mark it. Marks stay pending until you apply them.
  4. To drop a pending mark, select it and click Remove this mark.
  5. Apply a mark with Apply in its selection menu, or all pending marks with Apply Redactions in the panel. Save Changes applies any pending marks and saves the file.

/Tools/Security.title: Signing and security tools
/Tools/Security.description: Tools for signing PDFs, protecting them with passwords and permissions, and checking or removing signatures.
/Tools/Security.article:
User guide

Signing and security tools

In the tool picker, these tools sit under Signing, Document Security, Verification and Removal.

Signing#

  • Sign - draw, type or upload a signature and place it on the page. See Sign.
  • Sign with Certificate - add a digital signature that proves who signed and shows if the file is changed later. See Certificate signing.
  • Timestamp PDF - add a trusted RFC 3161 timestamp that proves the PDF existed at a point in time. See Timestamping PDFs.

Document security#

  • Add Password - set a User Password (needed to open the file) and an Owner Password (controls what people can do once it's open).
  • Change Permissions - allow or block printing, copying, editing, form filling and other actions.
  • Add Watermark - stamp text or an image across the pages.
  • Add Stamp to PDF - add a text or image stamp at a set position. See Content and editing.
  • Sanitize - remove JavaScript, embedded files, links, metadata and fonts.
  • Flatten - merge form fields and other interactive elements into the page so they can't be edited.
  • Unlock PDF Forms - make read-only form fields editable again.

Verification#

  • Validate PDF Signature - check who signed, whether their certificate is trusted and whether the file changed after signing. See Validating signatures.
  • Get ALL Info on PDF - show the PDF version, fonts, page sizes, permissions, metadata and more, as tables or JSON.

Removal#

  • Remove Password - unlock a protected PDF. You need the current password.
  • Remove Certificate Sign - strip digital signatures, for example so you can edit a signed file.

To black out text or areas for good, use Redact.

/Tools/Security/Certificate-Signing.title: Certificate signing
/Tools/Security/Certificate-Signing.description: Sign PDFs with a digital certificate, check existing signatures and add trusted timestamps.
/Tools/Security/Certificate-Signing.article:
User guide

Certificate signing

A certificate signature proves who signed a PDF and shows if anyone changes it afterwards.

On a self-hosted server, an admin sets up the server certificate, which certificate authorities count as trusted, revocation checks and the allowed timestamp servers (Signing certificates and trust).

Sign with a certificate#

  1. Open your PDF and pick Sign with Certificate.

  2. In Certificate source, choose where the certificate comes from. This step only appears when there is more than one option.

    • Upload - your own certificate file.
    • Server - your organisation's certificate, held on the server.
    • This device - a certificate on your computer or a USB token. Desktop app only, see On the desktop app.

  3. For Upload, pick the Certificate Format, then add your files under Certificate Files and enter the Certificate Password if there is one.

    Format Files
    PKCS12 or PFX One .p12 or .pfx file
    PEM A private key (.pem, .der, .key) and a certificate (.pem, .der, .crt, .cer)
    JKS A Java keystore (.jks, .keystore)

  4. In Signature Appearance, choose Invisible or Visible. For a visible signature, set Reason, Page Number and Logo (No Logo or Show Logo). The box shows the certificate name, the date and the reason. Name and Location are saved in the signature details only.

  5. Click Sign PDF.

Good to know:

  • Expired or not-yet-valid certificates are refused.
  • PDF viewers show self-signed certificates as unverified.
  • For proof of when the file was signed, run Timestamp PDF afterwards.

On the desktop app#

The desktop app can sign with a certificate in the Windows certificate store, or on a USB token or smart card (PKCS#11). This works in Local Only and Stirling Cloud mode.

  1. In Certificate source, choose This device.
  2. Choose the type:
    • Windows certificate store (Windows only) - pick a Certificate from the list. Windows asks for your PIN when you sign.
    • USB Token - pick the PKCS#11 driver, enter the Token PIN, set Slot (optional) if needed, then click List certificates and pick one.
  3. Continue with Signature Appearance and click Sign PDF.
Warning

Tokens lock after a few wrong PINs. Check your PIN before you click List certificates.

Common drivers (OpenSC, YubiKey, SoftHSM2) are found automatically. For any other driver, set the STIRLING_PKCS11_LIBRARIES environment variable to its full path (comma-separated for several) and restart the app.

Validating signatures#

  1. Open the signed PDF and pick Validate PDF Signature.
  2. Optional: under Custom Certificate File X.509 (Optional), add a certificate (.cer, .crt, .pem or .der) to check the signatures against. It replaces the usual trusted certificate authorities for that check.
  3. Click Validate Signatures.

Each signature gets a status:

  • Valid - the signature is intact and the signer's certificate is trusted.
  • Valid, signer not verified (Unverified in lists) - the signature is intact, but a trust check failed. The result lists why.
  • Invalid - the cryptographic check failed.

You can download the results as a PDF report, CSV or JSON.

Timestamping PDFs#

Timestamp PDF adds a trusted RFC 3161 timestamp that proves the PDF existed at a point in time.

  1. Open the PDF and pick Timestamp PDF.
  2. In Select a TSA server, pick a Time Stamp Authority: DigiCert, Sectigo, SSL.com, FreeTSA, MeSign, or one your admin added. DigiCert is the default unless your admin changed it.
  3. Click Apply Timestamp.

Only a hash of the document goes to the timestamp server. Existing signatures stay intact.

User guide

Sign

Sign adds a visible signature only, which anyone can copy. To prove who signed and detect later changes, use Sign with Certificate.

Add a signature#

  1. Open your PDF and pick Sign from the tool picker.
  2. Under Your signatures, click New signature and create it on one of the tabs:
    • Draw - sign with a mouse, trackpad, pen or finger.
    • Type - type your name and pick a style. Tick Also save my initials to save your initials too.
    • Upload - add a PNG, JPG or WebP image. White backgrounds are removed automatically.
    • Phone - scan the QR code, sign on your phone, and the signature appears in the app.
  3. Tick Save to my signatures to keep it, and Make default if you want. Click Use signature.
  4. Click the PDF to place the signature. Place it as many times as you need, on any page. Drag a placed signature to move or resize it.
  5. Click Apply N signatures. The signed PDF replaces the original in your workspace.

Saved signatures#

  • To reuse one, pick it under Your signatures and click the page.
  • Signed in, you can keep up to 20 signatures. Without signing in, up to 10 are kept in this browser.
  • Admins can set Who can use it to Everyone to share a signature with all users. Shared signatures appear under Shared.

/Tools/Workspace/Files-and-Sharing.title: My files and sharing
/Tools/Workspace/Files-and-Sharing.description: Keep files on the server with the File library, organise them in folders, and share them with other users or by link.
/Tools/Workspace/Files-and-Sharing.article:
User guide

My files and sharing

Login required

The File library keeps your files on the server and lets you share them with other users.

On Stirling Cloud, guests can't store or share files. In the desktop app, sign in to Stirling Cloud or connect to a self-hosted server. On a self-hosted server, file storage is on by default, but an admin has to turn on sharing (File storage and sharing).

Open the File library#

Click File library in the left rail, or Browse all files & folders next to PDF Library in the file sidebar.

Use Filter by source to see where each file lives:

  • Cloud - stored on the Stirling server
  • Local - only stored in this browser
  • Shared - shared with you by someone else

Keep a file on the server#

  • From the workspace: open the file's More actions menu in the file sidebar and choose Upload to server. After you change the file, choose Update on server to save the new version.
  • In the File library: select files and choose Add to Stirling library…. Files you upload or drop while a server folder is open go straight into that folder.

Organise files#

  • Click New folder, then New folder on the server. Server folders are private to you.
  • Open a folder's menu to Rename it, add a New subfolder, change its color and icon with Appearance..., or Delete folder.
  • Drag files onto a folder in the tree on the left, or select them and choose Move to….
  • Open a file's Version journey to see earlier versions, open one in the workspace, or remove it.
  • When you delete a file that's both on this device and on the server, choose This device only, Cloud only or Everywhere.

Share a file#

Select the file in the File library and choose Manage sharing, or click Share in the toolbar above an open file. If the file isn't on the server yet, click Save to server & share first.

Each person or link gets a role: Editor (the default), Commenter or Viewer. Commenter and Viewer can open and download the file. Only the owner can replace the file, delete it or change who has access.

Share with a person#

Under Shared users, enter their Username or email and click Add.

They need an account on the server you're using (on Stirling Cloud, a Stirling Cloud account). Remove access at any time with Remove.

Share with a link#

Pick a Role, click Generate Link, then Copy.

Anyone with the link must sign in before they can open it. They can then click Open in Stirling PDF or Download. Links expire after a set number of days (on a self-hosted server an admin sets this, 3 by default). To stop a link working, click Remove link.

To see who used a link, click View activity. It lists each person, whether they Viewed or Downloaded the file, and when.

/Tools/Workspace/Keyboard-Shortcuts.description: Default keyboard shortcuts for tools and the PDF viewer, and how to change them.
/Tools/Workspace/Keyboard-Shortcuts.article:
User guide

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use ⌘ for Ctrl and ⌥ for Alt.

Tool shortcuts#

The tools in the picker's Quick access list get Ctrl + Alt + 1 to 8 by default, in list order:

Shortcut Tool
Ctrl + Alt + 1 PDF Text Editor
Ctrl + Alt + 2 PDF Multi Tool
Ctrl + Alt + 3 Merge
Ctrl + Alt + 4 Compare
Ctrl + Alt + 5 Compress
Ctrl + Alt + 6 Convert
Ctrl + Alt + 7 OCR / Cleanup scans
Ctrl + Alt + 8 Redact

Other tools have no shortcut until you add one. Shortcuts are saved in this browser (or in the desktop app on this computer), so they don't follow you to other devices.

Change a shortcut#

  1. Open Settings → Preferences and expand Keyboard Shortcuts.
  2. Find the tool and click Change shortcut.
  3. Press the new key combination, or press Esc to cancel.

A shortcut must include Ctrl, Alt or ⌘. Shift on its own doesn't count. If another tool already uses the combination, you'll see Shortcut already used by and the tool's name.

To go back to the default, click Reset. For a tool with no default, Reset removes the shortcut.

PDF viewer shortcuts#

Print, select all and zoom work whenever the viewer is open. The rest work while your pointer is over the viewer.

Shortcut Action
Ctrl + P Print
Ctrl + A Select all text
Ctrl + = or Ctrl + + Zoom in
Ctrl + - Zoom out
Ctrl + 0 Fit to width
Ctrl + F Open or focus search
Ctrl + S Save changes
Ctrl + Z Undo
Ctrl + Shift + Z or Ctrl + Y Redo
Home / End First / last page
Page Up / Page Down Previous / next page
Esc Close search

With the Rotate tool open, press ← to rotate left and → to rotate right.

Desktop app shortcuts#

Shortcut Action
Ctrl + S Save the selected files to disk, or all files if none are selected. Files that didn't come from disk open a Save As dialog.
Ctrl + N Open a new empty window (Windows and macOS only).
Ctrl + R / Ctrl + Shift + R Rotate the view in the viewer clockwise / anticlockwise.

/Tools/Workspace/Page-Editor.title: Workspace and Page Editor
/Tools/Workspace/Page-Editor.description: How the workspace keeps your files between tools, and how to edit pages visually in the Page Editor.
/Tools/Workspace/Page-Editor.article:
User guide

Workspace and Page Editor

Add your files to the workspace once, then run as many tools on them as you like. The Page Editor lets you edit their pages as thumbnails.

The workspace#

  • Drag files onto the app or click Add files. They appear in the file sidebar under PDF Library.
  • Workspace files are kept in this browser (in the desktop app, on this computer). To keep a file on the server or share it, see My files and sharing.
  • After a tool runs, click Undo to restore the files as they were.
  • Each tool run saves a new version of the file. To see earlier versions, open the file's More actions menu in the sidebar and choose Version history. From there you can open an earlier version in the workspace or remove it.

Edit pages in the Page Editor#

  1. Open Page Editor from the top bar, or pick PDF Multi Tool in the tool picker. Each file gets its own row of page thumbnails.
  2. Select pages with their checkboxes, with Select All, or with Select by Page Numbers.
  3. Change the pages:
    • Drag pages to reorder them, or drop them into another file's row.
    • Hover over a page for Move left, Move right, Rotate left, Rotate right, Delete page and View page.
    • Hover between two pages for Split here or Insert blank page.
    • For several pages at once, use Rotate selected pages left, Rotate selected pages right, Delete selected pages, Insert blank pages after selected pages or Split after selected pages.
  4. Use Wrap pages, Zoom in and Zoom out to change the view, and Undo and Redo if you change your mind.
  5. Click Save changes to all files to apply your edits.

To run the same steps on many files, use Automate.

/Tools/Workspace/Processing-Folders.description: Turn a folder in the File library into a processing folder that runs a preset on every file you add.
/Tools/Workspace/Processing-Folders.article:
User guide

Processing folders

Login required

A processing folder runs the same processing on every file you put in it, for example classifying documents (My files and sharing).

Processing folders are personal: only you can see them. Presets marked Requires AI engine only work when AI is available. On Stirling Cloud, processing uses your team's credits (Plans, credits and billing).

Set up a folder#

  1. Start from either place:
    • Click Process a folder in the left rail.
    • In the File library, open a folder's menu and choose Process files in this folder.... This skips step 2.
  2. Choose the folder. Pick one under Server storage, or create a new one, then click Choose processing.
  3. Pick a preset and adjust its settings (what each preset does).
  4. Click Enable processing.

Files already in the folder and any you add later are processed on the server. The folder shows how many files are Ready, Processing, Failed or Queued.

Manage a folder#

Open the folder's menu in the File library:

  • Edit processing... - change the preset or its settings, then click Save changes. Saving replaces the folder's current processing.
  • Pause processing / Resume processing - stop and restart processing new files.
  • Retry failed files - run failed files again.
  • Restore all originals - put back the original of every processed file. Processing is paused until you resume it. To restore one file, use Restore original on that file.
  • Remove processing - turn the folder back into a normal folder.

In the desktop app#

Sign in to Stirling Cloud or connect a self-hosted server first (Connection modes).

  • To use a folder on your computer, choose On this computer in the setup. The app watches that folder while it's running and signed in, and sends new or changed PDFs to Stirling Cloud or your server for processing.
  • Try processing your downloads folder classifies the PDFs already in your Downloads folder and opens the results in the app. The files in Downloads aren't changed.

/Tools/Workspace/Read-and-Annotate.title: Read and annotate
/Tools/Workspace/Read-and-Annotate.description: Read PDFs in the viewer and add highlights, drawings, shapes, comments and notes.
/Tools/Workspace/Read-and-Annotate.article:
User guide

Read and annotate

Open a PDF in the viewer to read it, search it and mark it up. Two tools open the viewer:

  • Read (under Document Review in the tool picker) opens the file for reading and commenting. You can also click Reader in the left rail.
  • Annotate (under General) opens the viewer with the annotation tools in the side panel.

Viewer#

  • Switch between Single Page View and Dual Page View.
  • Open the Bookmarks, Attachments and Comments sidebars.
  • Search the text, select it and click Copy.
  • Print with Print PDF.

For shortcuts, see Keyboard shortcuts.

Annotation tools#

Group Tools
Text Markup Highlight, Underline, Strikeout, Squiggly
Drawing Pen, Freehand Highlighter
Shapes Square, Circle, Line, Polygon
Comments Comment, Insert Text, Replace Text
Notes & Stamps Text box, Note, Add Image

Use Select and Edit to move, resize or change an annotation you've placed.

To sign a PDF, use Sign instead.

Comments#

The Comments sidebar lists comments by page, in reading order. From there you can:

  • reply to a comment
  • click Locate in document to jump to it
  • search comments
  • remove every comment with Clear all comments (annotations stay in the document)

Save your changes#

Click Save Changes or press Ctrl + S. Annotations are saved as standard PDF annotations that other readers can show.
